title: Introduce interim schema coercion layer for tool-streaming backward compatibility
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a runtime-coercion middleware that safely rewrites streaming tool-call envelopes from legacy v1 schema to v2 shaped envelopes, gated behind a feature flag. No user-visible breaking changes expected; opt-out via X-Redwood-Prefer-Schema header.
description: Motivation: Several customers and internal SDKs are still emitting the legacy tool-call envelope (v1) while the new schema (v2) for streaming/tool-calls has been rolled out. This mismatch leads to two classes of instability: (1) streaming parser errors during tool/function call handoffs, and (2) partial structured-output fragments that leak into downstream tool orchestration. This PR adds an interim coercion layer in the API gateway/runtime that detects client-declared schema preferences, validates incoming streaming frames, and rewrites v1 tool envelopes into the v2 canonical shape at the stream boundary. The coercion is conservative and reversible: we inject a small per-request flag into request metadata (schema_coercion_applied) and emit telemetry when we rewrite frames. The middleware supports three modes: passthrough (no rewrite), permissive-coerce (rewrite v1->v2 and allow both response modes), and strict (reject unexpected envelopes). Default rollout: permissive-coerce behind the feature flag feature/schema-coercion-v1 with opt-out via the X-Redwood-Prefer-Schema header. Implementation details: - Negotiation: the middleware checks X-Redwood-Prefer-Schema and Accept-Schema headers, then consults the request's declared content-type. If client requests v2 explicitly, we do not coerce. - Streaming rewriter: a small streaming-state machine that transforms v1 tool-call open events into v2 tool_call.start frames, lifts argument envelopes into v2-typed 'args' fields, and ensures chunked structured outputs are framed as complete JSON tokens before forwarding to the model runtime. The rewriter supports partial-kv caching to avoid reserializing large arguments. - Tool-call fallback: for tool invocations where the model returns tool call frames in v1, we translate them to v2 for internal routing; when routing to legacy tool runners that only accept v1 we convert back at the tool adapter boundary. - Telemetry & tracing: new counters schema_negotiation.rewrites, schema_negotiation.rejections and per-route timing metrics added to the console. We emit a deprecation warning header (X-Redwood-Schema-Deprecation) when we detect v1 clients to drive SDK updates. Tests & rollout: unit and integration tests cover streaming reassembly, partial argument buffering, and back-to-back tool-calls. Canary deployment in us-west-2 for 24 hours, followed by region-by-region ramp controlled by the feature flag. Monitoring dashboards added and alerts created for rewrite error rate > 0.1% or client-perceived latency regression > 20ms. Backwards compatibility: users can opt into strict mode via feature flag to force schema errors. The middleware is temporary and will be removed after the v1 sunset window (communication via deprecation header + Linear/Jira). See below for changed files, commit summaries, and review notes.

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: This direction looks good, but the streaming state machine needs clearer invariants around partial JSON chunks — can you add assertions to ensure we don't emit malformed tokens?

Maya Patel (author): Added buffer invariants and unit tests that assert that partial frames never reach the router. Also added a safety timeout for in-flight partial arguments to avoid forever-waiting streams.
Rina Gupta: Please clarify how this interacts with KV cache eviction and token accounting — if we rewrite frames, do we double-count tokens?

Maya Patel: We only rewrite envelope metadata; token accounting occurs post-rewrite against the normalized payloads. Added metric schema_negotiation.token_delta to track any accounting delta and a test that ensures delta==0 for rewrite paths.
Sophie Keller: Suggest adding a tight canary (5% requests) in addition to region canary so we can verify SDK ecosystems before global rollout.
Maya Patel: Updated rollout plan to include 5% canary via the feature flag and added console chart for canary-specific rewrite rates.
ci_summary: All CI checks passed. OBS-integration streaming test failed on first run due to a flaky network partition scenario; test was re-run and passed. Lint and static analysis OK. Load test (small) showed 1.4% p99 latency increase under permissive-coerce at peak; flagged and monitored but accepted for rollout with a mitigation task ENG-2410.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-09-25. Squash message: 'Introduce interim v1->v2 schema coercion middleware to stabilize streaming tool-calls during migration. Add tests, metrics, and rollout config.' Deployed to canary in us-west-2 immediately after merge behind feature/schema-coercion-v1 flag.
